sentences.text: Pre-operative multi-sequence MRI: axial T1, contrast-enhanced T1 (T1ce), T2 and FLAIR, co-registered, skull-stripped and resampled to 1 mm isotropic (BraTS preparation).
No necrotic / non-enhancing core exceeds the volume threshold (confidence 0.66). This finding is low-confidence and is hedged accordingly.
The whole-tumour mass is predominantly left-sided (confidence 1.00).
An enhancing tumour component is present (confidence 1.00).
Whole-tumour burden is assessed as medium (volume tercile fitted on the training split; confidence 0.86).
The enhancing fraction of the whole tumour is mid (ET/WT tercile fitted on the training split; confidence 0.63). This finding is low-confidence and is hedged accordingly.
Acquisition quality (cjv, efc, snr, sharpness, inu, contrast, entropy) is substantially outside the training cohort range (mean |z| = 1.08); this case is a known weak point of the system.
T1 and T1ce show a hyperintense lesion with a central area of low signal intensity on T1 and high signal intensity on T1ce, consistent with a lesion of low signal intensity on FLAIR and T2 imaging.
There is no mass effect or midline shift visible on any of the sequences.
Automated release: case confidence 0.66 meets the calibrated gate threshold 0.55.
Key findings: ncr_present absent (p=0.66); laterality left (p=1.00).
